text: emma: Heads-up: links to headings that include inline code or trailing emoji are not resolving after the MDX roll. Example: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk#node-client-setup doesn't jump. rory: Huh. Can you paste the minimal snippet? emma: From /sdk/clients.md: ```markdown ### Node client setup (v2) :sparkles: Run `npm i @redwood/client` then init. ``` When built, the id becomes `node-client-setup-v2-1` and old links to `#node-client-setup` 404. priya: I can repro locally. The slugifier strips/normalizes inline code and emoji differently under the new MDX parser, then dedupes if similar slugs already exist. jules: CI linkcheck output: ``` [linkcheck] ERROR: Fragment not found: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk#node-client-setup (status: 200) [docusaurus] ERROR in plugin-content-docs: anchor not found for marker "#node-client-setup" ``` rory: Short-term fix: insert an explicit HTML anchor before the heading or use explicit slug syntax if supported (e.g. `### Node client setup {#node-client-setup}`). Which feels less invasive? emma: I prefer explicit id on the heading line when supported, but our parser doesn't accept the brace syntax consistently across mkdocs/docusaurus. So quick fix = HTML anchor right above heading: ```html ### Node client setup (v2) :sparkles: ``` This restores compatibility without changing visible text. priya: I'll open a small PR with anchors for the top 8 high-traffic SDK pages that contain inline code or emoji in headings. I'll also add a migration note to docs/migration/MDX-HEADING-CHARACTERS.md explaining that inline code/emoji may affect slug generation. jules: Deploy preview posted by docs-bot: https://deploy-preview-1350--staging.docs.redwood.ai/sdk/clients (build 1350) :white_check_mark: Linkcheck now passes for that page. rory: Good. Long-term we should normalize slug generation: strip inline code markers and emoji consistently and treat them the same across our toolchain. Filing ticket DOCS-738 to unify slugify behavior and add unit tests for headings with backticks and emoji. emma: Thanks. After merge, let's run a full-site linkcheck and scan for headings containing backticks or emoji: `git grep -n "^### .*[`\u2600-\u26FF\u1F300-\u1F6FF]" docs/` (rough). priya: PR opened: redwood/docs#3399 — quick anchors + migration note (assigns: priya; reviewers: rory, emma). Will post linkcheck summary after CI completes. docs-bot: CI linkcheck summary (build 1350): 1 page fixed, 7 pages remaining with similar patterns; follow-up ticket created DOCS-738.
